professional.*

`README.md`) and render. The default chunks use dataset D1 so that the file renders as it is.

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false

# Find the repository root (the folder that contains R/helpers_general.R)
root <- normalizePath(".")
while (!file.exists(file.path(root, "R", "helpers_general.R")) && dirname(root) != root) {
  root <- dirname(root)
}
stopifnot(file.exists(file.path(root, "R", "helpers_general.R")))
source(file.path(root, "R", "helpers_general.R"))

library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(knitr)

set.seed(2026)
```

```{r}
#| label: read-data

# CHANGE THIS CHUNK to read your dataset. Default: D1 (population with groups G1 to G3).
data_dir <- file.path(root, "data-sim", "out")
if (!file.exists(file.path(data_dir, "population_pheno.csv"))) {
  stop("Simulated data not found. From the repository root run: ",
       "source('R/helpers_general.R'); ensure_sim_data()")
}
dat <- read.csv(file.path(data_dir, "population_pheno.csv"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
glimpse(dat)
```

## 3. Methods

(WRITE: the steps in order. Say where you split the data, what you selected or tuned inside the
training part, how many tests you ran and which correction you used, and which software.)

```{r}
#| label: partition

# Example: split BEFORE exploring or selecting anything. Keep the evaluation part for the end.
dat$part <- sample(c("train", "valid", "eval"), nrow(dat), replace = TRUE,
                   prob = c(0.6, 0.2, 0.2))
table(dat$part)
```

## 4. Results

```{r}
#| label: tbl-main
#| tbl-cap: "(WRITE: caption.) Simulated data for teaching purposes."

# Example: size and outcome rate by group (replace with your main result)
main_table <- dat %>%
  group_by(group) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), mean_trait = round(mean(trait), 2),
            disease_rate = round(mean(disease), 3), .groups = "drop")
kable(main_table)
```

(WRITE: what @tbl-main shows, in one or two sentences, and the assumption behind your reading.)

```{r}
#| label: fig-main
#| fig-cap: "(WRITE: caption.) Simulated data for teaching purposes."
#| fig-width: 6
#| fig-height: 4

ggplot(dat, aes(group, trait)) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = cesgen_blue[["light"]]) +
  labs(x = "Group", y = "Trait", caption = sim_caption()) +
  theme_cesgen()
```
